audit.why: Darius owning every lane stage with Kassadin taking 2+ items is the honest shape here, and 59.09% over 22 games is a scaling win rate rather than a lane one. The chart was left alone; the text now explains what actually changes.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bank levels - 6, 11, 16 are the lane' was paired with 'take the fifteen-second invitation', a number that belongs to no ability in this matchup.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s. Twenty-six seconds at rank 1 is the largest window either champion gets in lane, and Riftwalk's 5s means you get five blinks inside one of them.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, breakdown.cooldowns, report[9].t and loading now use 26s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told you to shield his poke: content.wants.you[1] said 'Use Null Sphere's shield to absorb his outer-ring Q poke' and dosFull[1].t said 'Q-shield right before his trade lands'. Null Sphere's shield absorbs MAGIC damage only, and every damage source Darius owns is physical or true - the shield reads zero in this matchup.
audit.why: Riot on Null Sphere: 'granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage'. Darius: Decimate and Hemorrhage are physical, Noxian Guillotine is true damage. The real defensive play is geometry - Decimate heals him only off the blade, so standing inside at the handle denies both the extra damage and the heal.
audit.corrected: Rewrote wants.you[1], dosFull[1].t, report[5].t, tradeBad and loading around the handle-versus-blade rule instead of the shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup as having no cooldown-sequencing advice, and every window read 'when Apprehend is down' with no duration.
audit.why: Apprehend 26s, Decimate 9s, Noxian Guillotine 120/100/80s and free to cast at rank 3 with its cooldown refreshed on a kill - that last clause is why a fed Darius can chain executes through a teamfight.

audit.whatIsWrong: Boots were listed as 'Mercs or Sorcs' and anti-heal was unattributed.
audit.why: Darius deals physical and true damage only, so Plated Steelcaps is the boot that matters, and the heal to cut is Decimate's blade heal off champions.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2].why used the generic 'E only charges when spells fly, so passive lanes starve your waveclear'.
audit.why: True and unusually relevant here: Darius's whole kit is three casts on 9s, 5s and 26s, so Force Pulse charges slowly in this specific lane - unlike against a mage.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are pure survival — Darius wins every melee all-in here and you have only Null Sphere's shield to answer it. Stay out of Apprehend (E) range and last-hit from max distance; the cell that kills you is an E pull into stacked Hemorrhage and a clean outer-ring Q. Note his Q geometry: the outer ring is where it deals full damage and heals him, so being shoved to the edge of it is the WORST place to be — don't trade there, just soak a tick of bleed and back off. Never greed a caster minion sitting next to him.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are pure survival - Darius wins every melee all-in here and Null Sphere's shield does not help, because it absorbs magic and he deals none. Stay outside Apprehend's 535 range and last-hit from max distance; what kills you is an E pull into stacked Hemorrhage and a clean outer-blade Q. Note his Q geometry: the outer blade is where it deals full damage and heals him, so being shoved to the edge of it is the WORST place to be - if you are caught, step in toward the handle. Never greed a caster minion sitting next to him.

edits.after: He out-bodies you at level 1 - his outer-blade Q and Hemorrhage bleed beat your lone Null Sphere, so just survive and last-hit.

notes: The most dangerous line in this file was 'Use Null Sphere's shield to absorb his outer-ring Q poke' - Null Sphere shields magic only and Darius deals purely physical and true damage, so a player following that advice takes the full trade thinking they are protected. Replaced with the real defensive play: Decimate heals and hits hardest on the outer blade, so step toward him rather than away. Kassadin's Void Stone also ignores unit collision, which makes standing inside him practical, though I kept that implicit rather than asserting how it interacts with his hitbox. Level chart left at Darius 6/7 despite the 59.09% flag - that number is Kassadin's scaling, not his lane, and 'Kassadin' is longer than 'Darius' so a side flip would fall outside the length band anyway.
